items.title: Grief-stricken mother of star footballer reveals AFL executive phone call
items.description: West Coast Eagles star Adam Hunter's mother Joanne Brown says AFL executive Laura Kane reached out to her, but the grieving mother says the phone call was "too little, too late".

items.title: Heavy rain forecast for south-east states triggers flood alert for 10 areas
items.description: A powerful winter cold front will cause a broad band of rain and strong winds to sweep across southern Australia during the coming days.

items.title: US yen intervention blindsides Europe, puts global economy on alert
items.description: Global economic policy now seems at the mercy of an exceptionally casual approach to information, scribbled on a notepad, awaiting an update on Scott Bessent's to-do list.

items.title: 'Once-in-a-lifetime' discovery found in a cave hidden beneath a paddock
items.description: There are very few places on Earth that remain untouched and unseen by humans. For true explorers, the final frontier is not a distant speck in the sky, it is the underground realm beneath our feet.

items.title: Alan Jones once ruled the airwaves. Now he's the one doing the listening
items.description: Alan Jones sat impassively, legs crossed, with a notebook and pen in hand as the first of six male complainants began testifying this week in his indecent assault trial.

items.title: As Trump swings between extremes, the Iran war has metastasised
items.description: The Middle East conflict isn't just widening, it's highlighting more vulnerabilities in the region.

items.title: Drugs, sex and explosive claims light a fire under gambling reform
items.description: The explosive evidence heard at a two-day inquiry into Labor's proposed crackdown on wagering advertising has proved a watershed moment for the increasingly friendless bill.

items.title: What is the 'singles tax' and is it real?
items.description: The singles tax has nothing to do with the ATO, it's the extra people pay when they can't split costs like rent, internet, insurance and other household bills the way couples can.

items.title: Deliberately misleading party name approved for Victorian election
items.description: A political party with a deliberately misleading name has been successfully registered for the Victorian election, aiming to redirect left-wing votes towards parties on the right.

items.title: Bodies of WWI and WWII diggers finally identified
items.description: The soldiers died on the same day, 24 years apart. The first fell in Europe towards the end of World War I and the second in the Pacific Theatre during World War II.

items.title: I was hacked. Here's the real story and what's happening next
items.description: ABC business reporter David Taylor was hacked on X and warns how easily it could happen to you.

items.title: Thai PM flags gun control measures after 14yo kills seven
items.description: At least seven people, including teachers and students, have died after a student opened fire at a school in Thailand.

items.title: Strikes at the country's largest port this weekend could cost millions
items.description: As unions begin 48 hours of industrial action at BHP's operations in Port Hedland, what makes the mammoth export facility so critical to Australia's economy?

items.title: From Chicken Fried to Kiwi sledge: How Aussies won historic Olympic gold
items.description: It may be 10 years since Australia won gold in women's rugby sevens at the Rio Olympics, but the impact of the victory will be felt for generations to come.

items.title: The unexpected day jobs of Australia's female footballers
items.description: The dual lives that female athletes have to balance to play at an elite level and have a career is often forgotten.

items.title: Tragic figure or traitor? New show looks at life of Bennelong
items.description: Bennelong sang the first Aboriginal song on English soil in 1793. His life and legacy is under the microscope in Jane Harrison's play Bennelong in London.

items.title: Retro game pinging, popping and buzzing as new generation has a ball
items.description: Tash Anderson has become Australia's top female pinball competitor since being roped into attending a social event three years ago.

items.title: Cory Doctorow thinks Australia should be worried about digital sovereignty
items.description: Cory Doctorow says the AI revolution promised by tech bros isn't inevitable but the bursting of an AI bubble is. He wants to remind us another future is possible.

items.title: Vulnerable community members push for Census recognition
items.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics has sent field officers to services helping people without permanent homes to ensure everyone can be counted in Tuesday's Census.

items.title: Gun owner candidate says signage rules make him a target
items.description: Candidates in Tasmania's election continue to feel exposed as election material such as advertisements, signs or pamphlets must include the "true name and address" of whoever produced them.

items.title: Five decades in the making, a Garma announcement has an eye to the future
items.description: Half a century after Aboriginal land rights in the Northern Territory were written into law, a Garma Festival announcement could usher in a next chapter. But what would it look like?

items.title: Police officer in alleged relationship with criminal 'lied' about her whereabouts
items.description: A man of "dubious character" who was under active criminal investigation was in an alleged relationship with a Tasmanian police officer who disclosed police information to him, an investigation has found.

items.title: Country drivers dig deep for man tackling 'catastrophic' pothole crisis
items.description: Victorian residents donate money to a man's mission to make crumbling country roads safer as they wait for government action.

items.title: Vulnerable patients fear implications of stoma nurse shortage
items.description: A stoma nurse helped David Platt feel comfortable after a significant medical procedure, but now South Australia's largest regional city is nearly without the service.

items.title: Landowners still rebuilding a year after deepest snowfall in 'living memory'
items.description: "A disaster in slow motion" is how an orchardist describes last year's snowstorm on the New South Wales Northern Tablelands. He says the clean-up is moving at the same pace.
